facts.text: Pecos National Historical Park preserves thousands of years of history, from early indigenous peoples to Spanish colonists, Mexican and Anglo armies, Santa Fi Trail travelers, and railroad tourists.
Forked Lightning Ranch began as a 1920s dude ranch and later served as a summer home for a Hollywood movie star and her husband.
The Pecos River, which flows northward from the Santa Fe National Forest, runs through the village and feeds the surrounding wilderness.
Pecos serves as an entry point for outdoor adventures in the Pecos Wilderness, offering hunting, fishing, hiking, and camping opportunities.
The park’s Junior Ranger Program lets kids earn a badge while learning about Pecos National Historical Park’s history and natural features.
